conclusion: A computational substrate sigma is a typed bounded polynomial-time computation context . It consists of: an instance family X_ sigma ; a size function on instances together with a bound N_ sigma , so that only instances of size at most N_ sigma belong to the bounded carrier considered here; a declared solver-prefix family, assigning to each bounded instance the finite trace shape that a polynomial-time computation may generate before the history is audited. A substrate is therefore the typed context in which instances, scale, and trace formation have all been fixed, rather than a language or a set of inputs.

\label{def:autonomous-lift}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate.  An
\emph{autonomous lift} on \(\sigma\) is a typed object
\[
  L=(\mathrm{gen}_{L},\sigma_{L},\mathrm{replay}_{L})
\]
with the following components:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\) is a deterministic polynomial-time
  history-generation procedure.  In plain terms, it is a deterministic
  polynomial-time algorithm that, given the substrate input and the
  prior trace data, extends the computation history by one audited
  step.
  \item \(\sigma_{L}:H_{\sigma}^{L}\to S\) is the internal-state
  readout of the lift, where \(S\) is the lift's finite typed state
  space.  The value \(\sigma_{L}(h)\) records the internal determining
  state of the procedure at the history \(h\).
  \item \(\mathrm{replay}_{L}\) is the all-input replay record for
  \(\mathrm{gen}_{L}\): an audited machine-index and
  time-certificate object that allows the same polynomial-time
  procedure to be reproduced on any input.  This is the audit-side
  bookkeeping supplied by the \(\mathsf{FATCD}\) discipline
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsII2026}.\footnote{The autonomous lift is
  realized in Lean by the autonomous-lift declaration listed in
  \Cref{app:formalization}; the Lean record exposes additional
  family-characterizing predicates beyond the components named in the
  definition above.  The narrowing-disclosure discipline is recorded in
  \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\end{enumerate}

\label{lem:csl-core}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate, let \(L\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\sigma\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) be
the trace-fingerprint loop class on \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\).  Assume the six
structural premises (a)--(f) above.  Then the following four clauses
hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Dissolution.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) holds
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then for
  every loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and every history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\),
  \[
    \Mclass{\ell.h}\neq\Mclass{h}
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \Qclass{\ell.h}\neq\Qclass{h}.
  \]
  Equivalently, the M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry fails: every
  M-class change is accompanied by a Q-class change.

  \item \emph{Preservation.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) fails
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then
  there exist a loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and a history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\) such that
  \[
    \LoopActionQ{\ell}{h}=\Qclass{h}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \LoopActionM{\ell}{h}\neq\Mclass{h}.
  \]
  The M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry holds.

  \item \emph{Degenerate.}  If \((\sigma,L)\) has no
  predictive witness content, then \(M_{\sigma}^{L}=Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) on the
  support of \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\), and the M-vs-Q distinction is vacuous.

  \item \emph{Strength-independence.}  Given the value of
  \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\), the dissolution or preservation
  status of the loop-action asymmetry does not depend on the strength
  class \(\StrengthClass{k}\) of the coupling function used inside
  the lift's generation procedure.
\end{enumerate}

the standard class \(P\).  The obstruction has three parts.
\begin{enumerate}

  polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs.  A
  single current class does not by itself define a language predicate
  over all input strings.

  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) identifies histories by equality of all declared
  polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the
  decision bit.  Two histories computing the same language may still be
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit
  bookkeeping observables differ.

  machines may decide the same language while producing different
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-observable histories on the same instance.  These
  histories can map to different current classes but to the same
  language predicate.
\end{enumerate}
